GPU rental rates keep rising even as more capacity comes online

Since January:

>  A100 rates are up 23%, from $1.30 to $1.60 per GPU-hour

>  H100 rates are up 25%, from $2.15 to $2.70

>  B200 rates are up 27%, from $4.40 to $5.60, after briefly moving above $6 in March

Even H200 pricing has increased from around $2.60 in May to roughly $3 today

It’s strong evidence that, so far, there are no signs of overbuilding and that, if anything, there is still a GPU shortage

The strength in A100 and H100 pricing is especially important. Better software and inference optimization are extending their useful lives and increasing the revenue generated per GPU, which could support depreciation schedules longer than three years
